source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 36: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 36, assume the model/tokenizer, runtime build, hardware, precision, scheduler, batching policy, sampling settings, arrival process, prompt/output-length distribution, load points, and correctness/SLO criteria are fixed and documented; conclusions apply only to those conditions. Hypothesis: at each prespecified offered load, candidate B changes paired TTFT, TPOT, queueing delay, throughput, and P99 latency versus baseline A in warm steady state without increasing errors or violating the P99 target. Define the effect threshold and confidence rule before testing. Run repeated randomized paired replays of identical requests on isolated, equivalently configured hosts, with a separate warm-up period; randomize A/B order and repeat across independent seeds or time blocks. Instrument admission and queue timestamps, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token time, every decode-token timestamp, completion, cancellation, timeout, retry, error, and rejection. Compute TTFT (including queueing and separately excluding it), TPOT from decode intervals, end-to-end latency, request/token throughput, queue depth and wait, saturation, and P50/P95/P99/P99.9; stratify by prompt length, generated length, concurrency, and offered load and report sample counts and confidence intervals. Capture GPU/CPU utilization and memory, batch composition, KV-cache occupancy/paging, OOMs/evictions, power/temperature, network, background load, versions, kernels, and configuration diffs. Check output correctness and retries so failed requests do not disappear from denominators. Likely confounders are workload drift, cache warmness, dynamic batching, prefill/decode interference, thermal throttling, host contention, load imbalance, and retry behavior. Roll back or stop promotion on correctness or error-rate regression, OOM/admission instability, or a prespecified P99 breach; investigate with an independent replay before generalizing.
risks: Tail latency and throughput are workload-, arrival-, scheduler-, and batching-dependent; uncontrolled changes invalidate comparisons.
Prefill/decode contention, retries, cache paging, thermal throttling, and host interference can shift metrics differently.
evidence_required: Exact deployment, workload mix, offered loads, warm-up policy, repetitions, event timestamps, correctness checks, and resource telemetry.
Paired uncertainty intervals and prespecified effect/SLO rollback thresholds, followed by an independent replay.
